title: Heathers at New World Stages #heathersmusical #heathersthemusical #ku...
transcript: Heathers being back at New World Stages in 2025 is a full circle moment, and I gotta say, the show holds up pretty well. A cult classic film turned cult classic musical, Heathers follows high schooler Veronica Sawyer navigating her venomous new clique and her even more venomous new boyfriend. Some have long critiqued the musical for sugarcoating the dark themes of the movie, and if you feel that way, you might not love this production. It's a dark comedy, but I feel like sometimes the tone is too much comedy, not enough dark. Nevertheless, the score by Laurence O’Keefe and Kevin Murphy is still bangers, the writing is sharp, and it's a well-constructed show, especially with its almost airtight Act 1. With this production not being all that directorially different from the original bootlegs we all know and love, I spent most of the show appreciating the performances and the rock star cast that they've put together for this. The score is no joke — it's incredibly vocally demanding and everyone across the board was fantastic. Erin Morton's “Kindergarten Boyfriend” is insane, McKenzie Kurtz is a hilarious and elegantly ferocious Heather Chandler, and Casey Likes, though not having the edgiest presence, completely sold me on his J.D. with his vocals. The biggest excitement of the night was Kuhoo Verma making her debut as Veronica. The energy in the room for her was wild and she was absolutely amazing — her vocal clarity is unparalleled and she brings a vulnerability to the role that makes her character progression especially satisfying. I thought she and the rest of the cast were well worth the price of admission. With that, another program for my collection.
